# Risks

**Medium.** This adds an opt-in ambient path to the existing pendant insights route and memory. Risks are model cost accounting, digest idempotence, and derived-memory merge behavior. Ambient defaults off, server caps calls at 48/day, canonical citations are filtered after generation, and current conversation scheduler tests remain green.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Extends the existing pendant insight pipeline, route, schema, prompt, and memory. No second store or scheduler is introduced.
- Adds ambient rolling extraction over only newly finalized canonical segment IDs plus a bounded finalized context tail.
- Handles late finalization across ordinal gaps using persisted processed IDs, so a pending segment is not lost when later finalized.
- Persists empty ambient checkpoints to avoid replaying quiet windows.
- Adds bounded all-day digest chunking and deterministic merge into one owner/agent/session/local-day memory.
- Adds grounded digest summary, nullable-owner action items, commitments, follow-ups, notable moments, people/topics/quotes, and canonical citation filtering.
- Adds server-derived user-local day identity from the trusted runtime `TIMEZONE` setting.
- Adds deterministic normalized-content dedupe with server-recomputed keys and merged citations.
- Enforces min 8 segments, 300-second cadence, and a server-clamped 48-call daily LLM budget before calls begin. Multi-chunk digests reserve every chunk call atomically.
- Adds a synthetic all-day fixture mixing meetings, errands, casual chat, pending hypotheses, and eager rows.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature, opt-in and backward compatible by default.

# Documentation changes needed?

Part of #13432 — the **cloud route path** slice (claim: "Lane: [fable-hard-lane]", 2026-07-09): quota/cost preflight, conservative max-upload enforcement, resumable chunk-upload routes + progress state, retention, and batch delete — wired to the already-landed `@elizaos/import-conversations` core primitives (preflight #13901, resumable state #14266, artifact policy #14256). The core package is not modified.

## What this adds

**Routes** (`packages/cloud/api`, all org-scoped via `requireUserOrApiKeyWithOrg`):

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/imports/preflight` | Size + tenant-quota admission **before any bytes**; typed fail-fast DTOs |
| `POST /api/v1/imports/uploads` | Init resumable session (preflight → atomic quota reservation → batch row → R2 multipart → core session state) |
| `PUT /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId/chunks/:chunkIndex` | Digest-verified chunk append (offset/length/sha256 validated by the core primitive); idempotent duplicate retry; typed conflict |
| `GET /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId` | Progress + exact missing byte ranges (resume support) |
| `POST /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId/complete` | Whole-or-nothing: missing chunks ⇒ typed `upload_interrupted` with missing ranges — **never a silent partial import**; idempotent retry |
| `DELETE /api/v1/imports/uploads/:sessionId` | Abort: R2 multipart abort + quota release, idempotent |
| `POST /api/v1/imports/uploads/direct` | Small exports within the conservative direct ceiling; `resumable_required` above it |
| `GET /api/v1/imports/batches`, `GET/DELETE /api/v1/imports/batches/:batchId` | Batch inspection + retention-policy batch delete with per-artifact accounting |
| `GET /api/cron/cleanup-expired-import-uploads` | Retention sweep (registered in the `0 */6 * * *` cron fanout) |

**Use-case layer** (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/conversation-imports.ts`): all business logic lives here; routes only validate shape and return DTOs (`importFailureHttpStatus` maps stable codes → status). Storage quota rides the existing `org_storage_quota` atomic reserve/release; reservation is transferred to the raw artifact at complete, released exactly once on abort/expiry/delete.

**Persistence**: new `import_batches` / `import_upload_sessions` / `import_artifacts` tables (migration `0175_conversation_imports.sql`), org-scoped repositories, optimistic-concurrency chunk state writes reconciled via the core `mergeResumableUploadSessions` primitive.

**Storage**: `RuntimeR2Bucket` widened additively with the optional R2 multipart surface (fail-fast 503 when the binding lacks it — never buffer 1 GiB in Worker memory). Object keys follow the core artifact layout `conversation-imports/<tenant>/apps/<app>/batches/<batch>/<kind>/<sha256>.<ext>`.

**Config** (all optional, malformed values fail closed): `IMPORT_MAX_DIRECT_UPLOAD_BYTES`, `IMPORT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (defaults = core `DEFAULT_IMPORT_LIMITS`: 25 MiB / 1 GiB), `IMPORT_RAW_RETENTION_MS` (default = core 7-day), `IMPORT_MAX_EMBEDDING_UNITS`, `IMPORT_MAX_CONVERSATIONS` (per-import cost ceilings).

## Contract items covered (from #12071 / #13432)

- ✅ Object-store raw uploads with **short retention by default** (7-day `expires_at` marker + cron sweep; longer retention requires an explicit reason)
- ✅ **Content-addressed derived artifacts** tied to tenant/app/batch lifecycle (`storeDerivedArtifact`, dedupes identical content)
- ✅ **Tenant quota enforcement before import** (preflight + atomic reservation before any bytes)
- ✅ **Fail-fast typed errors** for quota/cost overrun (`quota_storage_exceeded`, `quota_embedding_exceeded`, `quota_conversations_exceeded`, `upload_too_large`, `resumable_required`)
- ✅ **Conservative configurable max upload size** by default
- ✅ **100MB–1GB imports require resumable chunks + preflight quota** (`requiresResumable`, direct path refuses with `resumable_required`)
- ✅ **Never silently truncate**: complete with missing chunks returns `upload_interrupted` + exact missing ranges; conflicting chunk retries are typed conflicts
- ✅ Batch delete/manage per retention policy with per-artifact success/failure accounting (retryable failures keep the batch alive)
- ✅ Failure DTOs for quota exceeded / upload interrupted / **parser failure** / **partial import** (`parser_failed`, `partial_import` are defined in the shared DTO union with required fields, ready for the executor — see seams)

## Remaining seams (explicitly out of this slice)

- **Import execution** (parse → redact → render → DocumentService → embeddings) consuming completed raw uploads: the step that will *surface* `parser_failed` / `partial_import` and charge **actual** embedding usage against tenant quota (this slice provides the per-import embedding/conversation cost ceilings + the post-parse gate hook via core `estimateBundleUsage`).
- **#13431 UI integration** (tracked separately; UI rows below are N/A).
- **Batch-delete planner core module**: claimed on the issue 2026-07-05 but never landed on `develop`; this slice implements delete accounting in the cloud service against the same semantics (idempotent, per-document accounting, retryable failures) without touching core. If that core module lands, the service loop can delegate to it.
- **Whole-file digest for resumable uploads** is client-declared at init (every chunk is server-side digest-verified by the core primitive; core's `buildImportArtifactDescriptor` hashes bytes itself, which a 1 GiB stream can't provide up front). `buildRawUploadStorageKey` mirrors the core key layout exactly and collapses into a core descriptor-from-digest variant if one is exported later. Direct uploads use the core descriptor with real bytes.
- `@elizaos/import-conversations` is wired via the established source-alias mechanism (tsconfig `paths` + `wrangler.toml [alias]`, same as `@elizaos/core`/`@elizaos/shared` deep aliases) rather than a `package.json` dependency edge — only the three pure core modules (`node:crypto` only) are aliased into the Worker bundle; parsers (node:fs) stay off it. No lockfile change.

Unified glassmorphic / liquid-glass look across the shell (chat, notifications,
menus, buttons) with REAL system glass on iOS 26 and graceful fallback
everywhere else. Design doc:
`packages/docs/ongoing-development/liquid-glass-unification.md`.

- [x] Based on the notification-shade branch tip (stacks on #15217).
- [x] 8 contract tests + full chat-sheet e2e PASS on the branch.

# Risks

Medium-low. The only live visual change is the chat + menu (flat card → glass
menu variant); everything else is additive library surface. The Swift plugin is
compile- and availability-gated to iOS 26 — on every current device/SDK it
reports unavailable and nothing changes.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

1. **`packages/ui/src/glass/`** — the glass system: five role-based variants
   (`sheet`/`card`/`pill`/`menu`/`banner`) in `tokens.ts` consolidating the ten
   divergent surface recipes found in the shell audit; `GlassSurface` primitive
   + `GlassStyles` (one stylesheet + refraction defs per document, mounted at
   the App root); `useNativeGlass` tier probe (`ios26-native` →
   `css-refraction` → `css-frosted`); exported through the `@elizaos/ui`
   barrel with NO static `@capacitor/core` import (server-safe, #15221).
2. **`GlassBridge` Capacitor plugin** (Swift + TS): real
   `UIVisualEffectView(UIGlassEffect)` anchored below a transparent webview at
   web-reported rects. `#if compiler(>=6.2)` + `if #available(iOS 26,*)` gates;
   typechecked against the real iOS 26 SDK on this machine. Registration
   mirrors `ElizaKeyboardBridge`. Capacitor stays on 8 stable — 9.0.0-alpha.5
   ships nothing glass-related (release notes quoted in the design doc).
3. **First migration**: the chat composer **+ menu** renders on the glass
   `menu` variant via a new `glass` prop on `DropdownMenuContent`.
4. Chat-sheet e2e extended: asserts `.eliza-glass-menu` is live and snapshots
   the open menu.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature (design-system foundation) + one visual migration.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/ui/src/glass/tokens.ts` (the vocabulary), then `GlassSurface.tsx`,
then `GlassBridge.swift`.

## Detailed testing steps

```bash
bun run --cwd packages/ui test -- --run src/glass/glass.test.tsx   # 8 tests
bun packages/ui/src/components/shell/__e2e__/run-chat-sheet-e2e.mjs # full suite + glass assertion
```

e5:T35f5,Implements the certification protocol from #14546 (epic #14541): verdict rollup, reviewer verdicts, Ed25519-signed `certification.json`, and fully-offline verification — the security-critical piece the develop→main CI gate (#14547) will call. Built on the `@elizaos/evidence` foundation from #14589 (merged).

> **Stacking note:** #14589 is merged into `develop`. This branch also carries the post-merge review-hardening commit from `feat/14552-evidence-bundle` (`c902a6a5fe6`: symlink-aware verify, `metaSha256` provenance binding, strict canonical objects, NFC paths) cherry-picked on top, because certification builds directly on those contracts. If that commit lands on `develop` through its own PR first, a rebase here dedupes it cleanly. **Consumed by #14547.**

## What + why

A pile of green lanes is not a promotion claim. This PR turns a finalized evidence bundle into a **signed, offline-verifiable statement**: *a keyholder reviewed exactly these verdicts over exactly this bundle for exactly this commit*. Everything the gate needs is in `packages/evidence` — the workflow in #14547 stays a thin caller with zero verification logic of its own.

New (ownership-scoped; additive-only outside `src/certify/**`):

- `src/certify/schema.ts` — strict certification contract (zod + frozen interfaces, mutually-assignable compile guards like the foundation).
- `src/certify/keys.ts` — node:crypto Ed25519 keygen, SPKI-DER sha256 fingerprints (first 16 hex), signing-key ingress (`ELIZA_CERT_SIGNING_KEY` PEM or base64-wrapped PEM, or `--key-file`). Nothing here writes or logs a private key.
- `src/certify/rollup.ts` — mechanical draft verdicts from lane `result.json` counters, `analysis.json` expectation failures, and caller-declared requirements (honest-skip: skipped/absent lanes fail unless marked optional-with-reason, then draft as `waived` carrying the reason).
- `src/certify/sign.ts` — `signCertification` / `verifyCertification` with distinct typed failure codes; the report lists **all** detectable failures, never first-failure-only.
- `src/certify/cli.ts` + package scripts — `certify:keygen | rollup | sign | verify`.
- `.github/certification/` — trust-model README (base-branch key rule, rotation, break-glass) written explicitly for #14547 to implement. The public-key PEM is deliberately NOT in this PR: the key custodian lands the production key in a dedicated reviewed PR (merging it is the act of trusting the key).

## Certification schema (`schema: 1`)

```ts
{
  schema: 1,
  bundleSha: string,      // sha256 hex of the bundle's manifest.json bytes
  commit: string,         // full 40-hex sha — short shas rejected
  branch: string,
  baseRef: string,
  tier: 'cpu' | 'gpu' | 'full',
  verdicts: [{ subject, verdict: 'pass'|'fail'|'waived',
               evidence: string[] /* bundle-relative */, notes? }],
  reviewer: { kind: 'agent'|'human', id, model? },
  createdAt: string, expiresAt?: string,
  signature: { alg: 'ed25519', publicKeyFingerprint, value /* base64, 64 bytes */ }
}
```

Signature = Ed25519 over `canonicalJsonBytes(payload-without-signature)` (sorted keys, no whitespace, one trailing newline — the foundation's canonical form). Parsing is **strict**: unknown top-level fields, unknown verdict values, absolute/traversal evidence paths, duplicate subjects, empty verdict arrays, and `waived` without non-empty notes are all rejected. Forward compat is a `schema` bump, never silent tolerance.

## Threat model (summary — full text in `.github/certification/README.md`)

- **The gate MUST read the public key from the BASE branch (`main`), never the PR head** — otherwise one PR swaps key + self-signed cert together. Key rotation = a reviewed PR replacing the pem; merging it is the act of trusting the new key.
- A valid signature proves a keyholder signed these verdicts over this manifest for this commit. `bundleSha` binds the manifest; the foundation's `metaSha256` binds `meta.json` (commit/branch/tier source) transitively — forging provenance after signing surfaces as `bundle-tampered`.
- It does **not** prove diligence; the reviewer identity is inside the signed payload for exactly that reason, and the gate should surface it in the check summary.
- `wrong-key` (different keypair) is distinguished from `bad-signature` (altered payload); forging the trusted fingerprint on a foreign signature moves the failure to `bad-signature` — the crypto check still holds (tested).
- Break-glass is **not a code path**: admin bypass of the required check, visible in the GitHub audit log. There is deliberately no flag or env var that skips signature checks.
- `certify:sign` refuses to sign a bundle that fails integrity verification, and the verifier hard-errors (rather than reporting "cert invalid") on a misconfigured trusted key so an attacker cannot induce a misleading outcome.

## Verify contract for #14547

```bash
bun run --cwd packages/evidence certify:verify -- \
  --cert <certification.json> \
  --pubkey <BASE-branch>/.github/certification/certification-public-key.pem \
  --expected-commit <pr-head-sha> --max-age-hours 72 --required-tier full \
  [--bundle <dir>] --json
```

Exit `0` iff valid, `1` otherwise. `--json` prints the full `CertificationVerifyReport` on stdout: `{ ok, failures: [{code, message, context}], payload?, certification?, bundle? }` with codes `schema-invalid | unsigned | bad-signature | wrong-key | stale | commit-mismatch | bundle-tampered | verdict-failures | tier-insufficient`.

## Key custody note for the repo owner

No key material ships in this PR — neither half. The key custodian (repo owner) generates the production keypair on a trusted machine, stores the private half as the `ELIZA_CERT_SIGNING_KEY` repo secret, and lands the public PEM (with its fingerprint) via a dedicated reviewed PR per `.github/certification/README.md`. Until then the gate (#14547) cannot be enabled; `certify:verify` has no default trust anchor and requires an explicit `--pubkey`.

Part of #14546 (protocol layer: `certify:keygen|rollup|sign|verify`). Still open on that issue: the unified `evidence:certify --tier` orchestrator entrypoint and the committed trust-anchor PEM.

e6:T223e,## What + why

Adds the tiered heuristic **analyzer registry** to `packages/evidence` (#14542, epic #14541). An analyzer is a pure `(input, ctx) -> status-bearing fragment` that declares which artifact kinds it consumes and which tier (`cpu`/`gpu`) it belongs to. A runner fans every applicable analyzer over every visual subject in a bundle and writes ONE `analysis.json` per subject **beside its pixels**, with an honest per-analyzer status:

- `ran` — executed and produced data
- `skipped-tier` — analyzer tier above the run tier (e.g. gpu analyzer on a cpu run)
- `skipped-missing-tool` — required binary / endpoint / baseline unavailable
- `failed` — the analyze call threw (message captured; one broken analyzer can't fail the matrix)

No analyzer is silently dropped; no skip fabricates empty data (repo doctrine: "not loaded" must never read as "zero"). The registry is **data, not a plugin system** — a flat array + name lookup, no dynamic loading.

The four `visual-qa.mjs` primitives (OCR, palette, brand-rule fractions, size-agnostic change-metric) are ported with behaviour preserved and real tests added; the missing cheap heuristics from the issue are implemented.

> **Stacked on #14589** (foundation, merged to develop) and its post-review hardening commit on `feat/14552-evidence-bundle` (merged in here). Mark ready + rebase once that hardening lands on develop. All **97 foundation tests stay green** alongside the **39 new analyzer tests** (136 total).

## Analyzers

| name | tier | consumes (kinds) | output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ocr.tesseract` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | `{ engine, text, words, confidence }` (ported; `skipped-missing-tool` when tesseract absent) |
| `ocr.unlimited` | gpu | screenshot, keyframe | same shape via OpenAI-compatible `llama-server` (Baidu Unlimited-OCR, #14543); endpoint `ELIZA_GPU_VISION_URL`, `skipped-missing-tool` when unset/unreachable |
| `color.palette` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | dominant-k quantized swatches `{ hex, rgb, fraction }` (ported) |
| `color.corners` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | 4-corner + centre swatches `{ position, rgb, hex, bucket }` — wrong-theme / dark-mode bleed |
| `brand.rules` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | blue/orange/neutral fractions + brand verdict (orange-accent-only, no-blue) (ported) |
| `diff.change` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | size-agnostic change fraction + bbox (ported); baseline via `ctx.baselineResolver` |
| `diff.region` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | pixelmatch -> clustered changed-region bboxes `[{x,y,w,h,fraction}]` + per-region change/static assertions |
| `hash.perceptual` | cpu | screenshot, keyframe | 64-bit DCT pHash + Hamming/same-screen utils (no new dep — computed on sharp raw) |
| `tree.aria` | cpu | html-tree | node count + normalized snapshot; pure `normalize`/`diff`/`prune` exports (no Playwright dep) |
| `video.keyframes` | cpu | video | ffmpeg scene-cut + first/last frames -> emits `keyframe` artifacts under `video/keyframes/<slug>/`; image analyzers then fan over them |

**Engine indirection** (`OcrEngine = { id, available(), recognize() }`) lets one analyzer body serve tesseract, the gpu `unlimited` client, and `apple-vision`. The **Apple Vision** helper (`packages/app/scripts/ocr-vision.swift`, PR #14490) is merged in develop and wrapped as `AppleVisionOcrEngine` (macOS + swift, stdin NDJSON); it is exported but not yet in the default registry pending the consumer-migration follow-up (#14470).

**New dep:** `pixelmatch@^7` (was already a transitive dep). `sharp@^0.34.5` (repo-standard) added explicitly. Both appended to `package.json` without reordering existing keys.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>e7:T3071,## What

The context-retrieval pass + corpus-wide pseudonym consistency stage of the corpus PII scrub pipeline (stage position: between candidate-mining and the LLM-pass), built entirely on the landed rails — `PiiScrubService` (#14808 slice 1, PR #15139) and the `PII_SCRUB` model seam (#14809, PR #14980) — with **zero changes to either**. No new scheduler, no new queue, no second knowledge-graph store.

Closes #14805

### `packages/core/src/security/pii-pseudonym-map.ts` — one person = one replacement everywhere
- `CorpusPseudonymMap`: cluster-keyed (`entity:<entityId>` from the EntityStore alias backbone — **never surface strings**), extending the session pseudonymizer's deterministic minting (`mintSurrogate`, now exported) from per-session to corpus-persistent: mint seed is `(salt, kind, clusterId, attempt)`, salt persisted inside the (secret) snapshot, so the same person deterministically keeps the same pseudonym across runs, artifact types, and assignment orders.
- **Collision behavior:** two distinct people sharing a name are two clusters with two pseudonyms; an alias claimed by 2+ clusters is **ambiguous** — never blind-substituted (a longest-first self-mapping shields it from partial rewrites by contained shorter aliases), surfaced for model escalation with ALL candidate assignments. A newly learned real alias equal to an existing pseudonym re-mints that cluster with a `supersededPseudonyms` audit trail. Re-homing a platform identity to a second cluster **throws** — identity merges stay in the merge engine.
- **Idempotent upsert** (no duplicate clusters/aliases/identities on re-assign) and **pseudonym stability across ruleset bumps** — a `v<ruleset>` bump re-scrubs content (content-hash markers re-key) with the SAME pseudonyms, so a re-scrub never re-links identities.

### `packages/core/src/security/pii-pseudonym-map-store.ts` — the map is a secret artifact
- The alias→pseudonym map inverts the scrub, so it lives **outside the retrievable corpus**: one dedicated runtime-cache key (`pii:pseudonym-map:v1`, next to the scrub done-markers), never a document/memory row, no ingestion path — unreachable via `searchDocuments` / `searchMessages` / `searchMemories` / `SEARCH_KNOWLEDGE`, never chunked or embedded. Confidentiality is structural, plus at-rest AES-256-GCM (v2 settings-secret scheme, dedicated AAD `elizaos:pii-pseudonym-map:v1` for domain separation, `SECRET_SALT` lifecycle).
- **Fail-closed everywhere:** refuses to persist plaintext; wrong key, tampered ciphertext, non-ciphertext value, or a structurally invalid snapshot all **throw** (deliberately stricter than `decryptStringValue`'s return-original-on-error) — a partial map would silently re-mint pseudonyms for already-mapped people, which is worse than stopping the pipeline.

### `packages/core/src/security/pii-context-pack.ts` — the context-retrieval pass
- `assembleContextPack`: per chunk, resolves candidates through a **structural `EntityStore.resolve` seam** (`PiiEntityResolverStore` matches `packages/agent/src/services/knowledge-graph/entity-store.ts` field-for-field; `entityResolverFromStore(kg.getEntityStore())` wires it with zero adaptation — core does not import agent), gathers related fragments (`DocumentService.searchDocuments`, `runtime.searchMemories` under the embeddings throw-never-fabricate doctrine, `adapter.searchMessages` with explicit roomIds), clusters confident resolutions into the map, and emits the bounded pack + the per-chunk `{entityClusterId, surrogate, kind}` assignment slice — **never the whole map, never a real alias**.
- Failure doctrine: absent sources are structurally skipped and audited in `sourcesQueried`; a wired source that throws **propagates** (rails retry the item) — degraded context silently producing a wrong verdict is the failure mode this pass exists to prevent.
- `buildScrubRequestDraft` folds a chunk + pack into the landed `PII_SCRUB_REQUESTED` payload — the exported interface siblings (#14806 transcript anchors, #14807 audio redaction span labels) consume for corpus-consistent replacements.
- `pii-pseudonymizer.ts`: additive `export` on `mintSurrogate` + `compileReplacer` only; no behavior change (fuzz + unit suites green).

## Tests (all in this PR, 57 new; 113 green across the PII surface)

- `pii-pseudonym-map.test.ts` (25): deterministic stability across runs/orders/snapshot-reload; the **hard-gate** at map level (full name in a document, first name in a second document, nickname in chat, @handle in a transcript mirror → one pseudonym; similar-named second person → different one; zero alias survivals; idempotent re-substitution); ambiguity/collision/re-mint/identity-conflict; ruleset-bump × marker-key interplay; blocklist, regex-metachar + unicode aliases, word boundaries, empty/adversarial input; fail-closed snapshot validation.

e9:T1f50,Part of #14541. Closes #14544. **Stacked on #14589 (`feat/14552-evidence-bundle`)** — mark ready + rebase onto `develop` after that merges. The diff below is scoped against the foundation branch.

## What & why

Agent-invoked **VLM screenshot Q&A** in `packages/evidence`: a reviewing agent (claude/codex) generates targeted questions about a screenshot and gets **structured** answers back — the semantic layer (blue-fraction, OCR, diff regions) can't answer "is the Send button clipped?" or "is this the designed empty state or a blank panel?". Answers land in `qa.json` beside the pixels with full model + token-usage provenance so the certify reviewer (#14546) folds them into verdicts.

Runs **standalone in minimal containers** — no dependency on `@elizaos/*` plugin packages. Talks to the model APIs by direct `fetch` (the plugin conventions were read for the wire shapes, not imported).

### Design points
- **One request per image carrying ALL questions** — image tokens paid once; response forced to strict JSON `{answers:[{id,answer,confidence,details}]}`.
- **Strict parsing, no regex rescue.** A non-conforming response throws `VISION_RESPONSE_INVALID`; exactly **one** corrective retry is spent (and counted in `provenance.retries`) before failing typed. Never a fabricated answer.
- **NOT_CONFIGURED is a typed failure, never a default.** No key / base URL / explicit backend ⇒ `VISION_NOT_CONFIGURED` (keyless-env contract: explicit skip, never invented answers).
- **Downscale longest edge → 1568px** via sharp before base64 (Anthropic downsamples past that anyway); original + sent dimensions recorded.
- **Content-addressed cache** at `<bundle|cwd>/.vision-qa-cache/<sha256(image)>/<sha256(model+backend+questions-canonical)>.json` using the foundation's `canonicalJson` for the query key; `--no-cache` bypass; corrupt entry ⇒ miss.

### Backends (one interface, `VisionBackendClient`)

| Backend | Transport | Model default | Image | Key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | Messages `/v1/messages` | `claude-opus-4-8` | base64 block | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `openai` | chat.completions | `gpt-5.5` | `image_url` data-URI + `response_format: json_object` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `local` | chat.completions @ `ELIZA_VISION_QA_BASE_URL` | `qwen3-vl` | `image_url` data-URI | none (llama-server) |

`ELIZA_VISION_QA_BACKEND` ∈ `anthropic|openai|local`; default `anthropic` when key present, else `local` when base URL set, else NOT_CONFIGURED.

### Deliverables
- `askAboutImage(imagePath, questions, opts)` + `askBatch(entries, opts)` (inline p-limit, dependency-free; a per-entry failure rejects the batch — no silent drops). Anthropic Message-Batches API left as a documented seam, no stub.
- `suggestQuestions(analysis, {viewName?, expectations?})` — pure/deterministic; turns blue-over-threshold, large diff regions, and OCR dev-strings into targeted question drafts with stable ids.
- `writeQaRecord(bundle, subjectBundlePath, questions, askResult)` → kind `qa`, placed via `bundlePath` beside the subject (`visual/…/x.png` → `visual/…/x.qa.json`).
- CLI: `bun run --cwd packages/evidence vision-qa -- ask <image> -q "…" [--context analysis.json] [--backend …] [--json]` — `--context` runs `suggestQuestions` and merges ahead of `-q`.

### Foundation contract (absorbed the #14589 review-hardening)
Rebased onto `c902a6a5fe6` (symlink-aware verify, `metaSha256` provenance binding, strict-canonical objects). Impact confirmed: `writeQaRecord` builds plain-object/ISO-string records (`canonicalJson` no longer accepts Date/Map/class instances — pinned by a test), copies via `addArtifact` (no symlinks), and my `qa-record` test's `verifyBundle` still passes clean under the new verify.

# Risks

Low–medium. The notification surface is user-facing UI + a client-side delivery policy (no server contract change). # What does this PR do?

Completes the notification shade and hardens it against the review sweep.

**Shade UI (`NotificationsHomeCenter`)**
- **Priority-only triage** — the priority/recent sort toggle is gone (sort takes no mode; a test pins that it can't be flipped to recency).
- **Liquid-glass Z-stacked groups** — a multi-row view-group renders at rest as an iOS-style card stack: highest-priority card on top, up to two glass peeks beneath, the group size in the eyebrow.
- **Pull-to-expand / overscroll-collapse** — the "N more / Show less" buttons are gone; pulling down expands the shade (touch non-passive listeners, mouse pointer with capture, wheel-up), scrolling back up past the top collapses it. A visually-hidden toggle keeps it keyboard/AT reachable.
- **Single-open chromeless actions** — pressing a row opens its option strip and collapses every other row; options are bare action text (no pill fill, no border). Swipe-to-dismiss stays.

**Native-first delivery (`notification-store` + `native-notifications` + banner store)**
- OS-native surfaces own the alert on desktop (Electrobun `desktopShowNotification`) and mobile (Capacitor local/intent channels); the in-app glass banner is the web/fallback surface, with the browser `Notification` API only for hidden tabs — no more OS+banner double-alert.

**Review-sweep correctness fixes (this PR's new work on top of the landed shade)**
- Z-stack top card keyed by id — swipe-dismissing the top no longer promotes the next card into the outgoing card's fling-out state (invisible-card bug).
- Pull re-bases at the top crossing — a continuous drag that first scrolled the expanded list back to the top no longer arrives pre-maxed and instantly collapses.
- Mouse pull captures the pointer — release outside the narrow centered list still commits.
- `pullPx` reset on empty inbox; wheel accumulator decays after a quiet period (no render-time `Date.now()`).
- Outside-tap collapse exemption scoped to `[data-notif-row]`, not the whole `flex-1` chromeless center section — a tap on the bare field around the rows collapses the chat again.
- Interrupt surfaces coalesce by `groupKey` (banner queue, Capacitor id, web tag) the way the inbox does — a same-group burst shows one banner / replaces one tray entry, not N.
- Native bridge no longer fabricates `"local"` success when a required Android channel can't be created (Android 8+ drops a post to a nonexistent channel) — it falls through to glass.
- `hydrate()` failure logs (J1 boundary) instead of silently reading as an empty inbox; the independently-subscribed WS stream still populates it.

Features + bug fixes (non-breaking).

## What changed

## What

New `packages/evidence` (`@elizaos/evidence`, private, ESM, no framework dependency — it must run in minimal CI/vast containers):

- **`src/schema.ts` — frozen schema-1 contract.** `ArtifactEntry` / `BundleManifest` / `BundleMeta` + `ArtifactKind`/`RunnerKind`/`Tier` unions, exactly as specced in the issue. Explicit interfaces are the contract; zod validators are held mutually assignable at compile time so type and validator cannot drift. Reading untrusted manifests/meta from disk throws `EvidenceValidationError` with per-field issues (error-policy J3) — never a silently-repaired object. Path traversal (`..`, absolute, backslash, `.`/empty segments) is rejected at validation time.
- **`src/canonical.ts` — signed byte form.** Canonical JSON: keys sorted (UTF-16 code-unit order), arrays in caller order, no whitespace, UTF-8, exactly one trailing newline (part of the signed bytes). Non-representable values (NaN/Infinity/bigint/function/undefined-in-array) throw instead of degrading to `null`.
- **`src/bundle.ts` — builder + verifier.** `createBundle` opens `evidence/runs/<utc yyyymmdd-hhmmss>-<shortsha>-<tier>/`; `addArtifact` hardlinks (same volume) or copies (EXDEV fallback, annotated J4), hashes **as stored**, and places by a deterministic kind→family mapping (`lanes/<lane>/…`, `visual/<source>/…`, `video/…`, `trajectories/…`, `html-trees/…`, `misc/<source>/…`) with a `bundlePath` escape hatch for wave-2 analyzers to sit `analysis.json`/`qa.json` beside pixels. `finalize()` sorts artifacts by path and writes canonical `manifest.json` + `meta.json`, returning `manifestSha256` (the value certification signs). `verifyBundle(dir)` re-hashes everything and reports `missing` / `size-mismatch` / `hash-mismatch` / `unlisted` findings. Clock and runId are injectable → byte-stable manifests are testable. Bundle paths are NFC-normalized at ingress (macOS NFD vs linux NFC). `finalize()` writes+hashes `meta.json` first and embeds `manifest.metaSha256`, binding provenance into the signed envelope; `verifyBundle` is lstat-based and additionally reports `symlink` (symlinked artifact = mutable after signing; symlinked dir = unswept external tree) and `meta-mismatch` findings.
- **`src/provenance.ts`.** Commit/branch via `git rev-parse` (execFile, fails loud with a typed error outside a repo — no fabricated provenance); runner from `ELIZA_EVIDENCE_RUNNER` ∈ local|vast|ci (invalid value throws instead of downgrading), inferred `ci` from `CI` env, default `local`; env fingerprint is a small allowlist (node/bun versions, platform, arch, tier, TEST_LANE) — full env is never captured.
- **`src/ingest.ts` — 7 silo ingestors, producers untouched.** e2e-recordings, aesthetic-audit-output, device-e2e-output (both roots; the #14494 bundle-dir shape), packages/app/test-results, reports/walkthrough (+ app mirror), reports/live-test-runs, scenario-runner reports (+ reports/scenarios). Roots mirror `scripts/evidence-review/generate.mjs` DEFAULT_SCAN_DIRS. Each returns `{silo, status: 'ingested'|'absent', artifactCount}` — an absent silo and an empty silo are different results, never conflated.
- **`src/cli.ts` — thin.** `bundle:create -- --tier cpu|gpu|full [--out] [--repo-root]` and `bundle:verify -- <dir>`; all logic in the lib, J1 boundary translation at the process edge.
- Registered in the `server` test lane via `elizaos.scripts.testLanes` (verified in `run-all-tests.mjs --plan`).

  // bundle
  createBundle, EvidenceBundle, verifyBundle, formatRunId,
  // provenance
  collectGitProvenance, resolveRunnerKind, buildEnvFingerprint,
  // ingest
  ingestAllSilos, ingestNamedSilo, SILO_NAMES,
  // errors
  EvidenceError, EvidenceValidationError,
} from "@elizaos/evidence";
```

No deviations from the issue/spec schema. Two additions (additive, documented): `AddArtifactOptions.bundlePath` for exact placement (needed by #14542/#14544), and — from the fable review round — `BundleManifest.metaSha256` (required, 64-hex) binding `meta.json` bytes into the signed envelope so forged commit/branch/runner fails verification. Schema stays 1 (unreleased).

Deliberately **not** in this PR (hot-zone guard per the design doc — `scripts/evidence-review/**` has in-flight PRs): pointing `evidence-review/generate.mjs` at a bundle via `--bundle`. That lands with consolidation (#14550).

ed:T1f2a,## Voice UX — the complete V2a voice stack in one PR (supersedes #15417) [sol-cloud]

**This PR is now THE single voice-UX PR.** It contains the full **V2a chunked-segment streaming ASR core** (live incremental transcript) **plus** the hands-free auto-send + in-flow toggle + VAD-tunability layer, as one coherent change on `develop`. It **supersedes and closes #15417** — that branch's V2a streaming core is included here in its entirety (byte-identical segmenter/stitcher/segment core), so there is no longer a separate streaming PR to land first.

Design docs: `VOICE-STREAMING-DESIGN.md`, `VOICE-LOOP-DOSSIER.md`. Extends the #15267 VAD/silence-guard base; does **not** regress barge-in (#15353/#15327), mic-permission recheck (#15329), shared-tier voice (#15400). **No V2b websocket.**

---

### 0. V2a streaming ASR core (was #15417 — now included here)

- **Chunked-segment streaming transcription:** `cloud-stt-segmenter.ts` + `cloud-stt-stitcher.ts` cut speech into mid-utterance segments on length/pause boundaries and stitch them into a live incremental transcript, with seam-overlap dedup, silent-segment drop, and a graceful batch fallback when streaming isn't available. `local-asr-capture.ts` / `local-asr-transcribe.ts` drive the capture + per-segment transcribe legs; `voice-capture-factory.ts` wires backend selection.
- **Opt-out:** `client-types-config.ts` `asr.streaming` opt-out + the `server-cloud-tts.ts` change are identical to what #15417 shipped (confirmed byte-for-byte).
- Teardown/suspend/barge-in abort the in-flight segment POSTs (single `AbortController` per turn); a mid-utterance segment never submits — the turn's real final is committed at stop (stitched or batch fallback).

### 1. Hands-free auto-send (full path, DEFAULT OFF)

The complete end-of-speech → finalize → send path, hands-free. Ships **default OFF** — composer review is the launch default — gated behind a user preference (`autoSend`, defaults `false`).

- `applyTranscriptUpdate` (useVoiceChat) auto-sends a finalized **compose / push-to-talk** transcript when `autoSend` is on **AND** it clears the min-transcript reliability guard. Off ⇒ the transcript fills the composer draft for review. `passive` (ambient) auto-sends as before.
- **No double-send:** the auto-send path clears the transcript buffer, so an explicit `stopListening({submit:true})` cannot re-emit. Test-covered.

### 2. In-flow toggle on the mic surface

A compact lucide icon-button rendered **inside the composer, adjacent to the mic** — `AutoSendToggle`. Not a settings page.
- OFF (review): `PenLine`, `text-muted`. ON (auto-send): `Send`, `text-accent`. `aria-pressed`, disabled support, `data-*` hooks, richer Tooltip.
- Persisted via `saveVoiceAutoSend`/`loadVoiceAutoSend` (key `eliza:voice:auto-send`, default `false`), owned in `ChatView`.

### 3. VAD tunability

- **`vad-params.ts` — single source.** The end-of-speech tunables re-export the runtime `DEFAULT_LOCAL_ASR_AUTO_STOP` so there is exactly ONE runtime source (a test asserts they never drift). Auto-send guard params (`minChars`/`minWords`/`minSpeechMs`) owned here too.
- **`vad-debug.ts` — dev/QA affordance, OFF by default** behind `ELIZA_VOICE_VAD_DEBUG` (mirrors `tts-debug.ts`): logs each VAD decision + which threshold triggered the cutoff + the guard result.
- **`auto-send-guard.ts` — the reliability gate.** Pure `passesAutoSendGuard`: never auto-send empty / single-token / sub-threshold-duration noise.

## What this adds

**Span production — `@elizaos/shared/audio-redaction` (pure, browser+node safe)**
- `matchPiiSpansToWords`: text-PII verdicts (the `span` strings from tier-0 detectors / `PII_SCRUB` verdicts, with optional pseudonym labels from #14805 accepted as plain input) are located inside **raw timed-ASR word spans** (`TranscriptWord` — no dependency on #14806's unlanded anchor seam). Matching is separator-insensitive in both directions: `"John Smith"` across two ASR words and `"555 0123"` inside one fused ASR word `"5550123."` both match; **every** occurrence is windowed. Unlocatable PII returns in `unmatched` — the caller must fail typed (fail-closed, per @LauraGPT's acceptance note); it is never silently empty.
- `mergeRedactionSpans`: pad → clamp to `[0, duration]` → merge overlaps/adjacency/containment into non-overlapping integer-ms windows; malformed spans **throw** rather than drop. Default pad is **250 ms, empirically calibrated** (see evidence: at 150 ms a boundary digit fragment of the planted phone number survived; at 250–300 ms nothing PII-shaped survives re-transcription).

**Execution — `packages/agent/src/api/audio-redaction.ts`**
- **Pure-TS PCM16 WAV lane** (every runtime, no ffmpeg): sample zeroing (mute) / phase-anchored 1 kHz sine (bleep). Byte geometry untouched, so duration is preserved **exactly** and output is **bit-deterministic**. This covers the voice pipeline's native 16 kHz PCM16 WAV with zero dependencies — the constrained-runtime criterion.
- **ffmpeg lane** (desktop/server only) for ogg/opus, m4a/aac, mp3, webm using the issue's empirically verified graphs — `volume=0:enable='between(t,S,E)+…'` (mute), `sine=f=1000` + gated `amix=duration=first:normalize=0` (bleep) — with `-bitexact` for deterministic bytes. Per-container duration assertions: wav+ogg exact (±2 ms probe slack), aac/mp3 ±(1024/sampleRate)s (one encoder frame); drift beyond tolerance throws `AUDIO_REDACTION_DURATION_DRIFT`. A lossy container on a host with **no ffmpeg** (mobile/workers) throws typed `AUDIO_REDACTION_UNSUPPORTED` — observable, never a silent skip.

**Storage — `packages/agent/src/api/audio-redaction-store.ts` (#8876-clean)**
- The redacted variant is **a second object in the ONE content-addressed media store** (`persistMediaBytes` → `${STATE_DIR}/media/<sha256'>.<ext>` served at `/api/media/<sha256'>.<ext>`). No new store, no files table, no `fileId`, no refcount engine. Job key `pii-audio:<originalSha>:v<ruleset>:<mode>:<spanHash>` (the audio analog of the #14808 `pii:<sha>:v<ruleset>` marker). A small capped memo (`audio-redactions.json`, the `background-pins.json` precedent) makes re-runs cheap lookups — it is a cache, not truth: wiping it recomputes to the **identical output sha** (tested). `media-store.ts` gains two additive exports (`storedMediaFileExists`, `mimeForStoredMediaFile`); nothing else in the store changes.

**Verify — `@elizaos/shared/audio-redaction-verify` + agent adapters, deliberately SEPARABLE from the span producer** (per the acceptance note):
- `RedactionTranscriber` contract: audio bytes + language hint in, normalized transcript out, **no timestamps required**. Judgment = PII absence by normalized fuzzy containment (never transcript equality — whisper hallucinates filler over silence) + sentinel presence (over-mute guard). **Zero configured verifiers throws typed** — never a vacuous pass; a backend throw propagates.
- Adapters: `runtimeTranscriptionTranscriber` (registered `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION`, interim purpose), `openAiCompatSttTranscriber` (any self-hosted `/v1/audio/transcriptions` — faster-whisper/FunASR/SenseVoice, the independent-verifier lane), and `energyFixtureTranscriber` (deterministic, model-free RMS + 1 kHz Goertzel over the real bytes, for no-ASR environments; honestly a fixture — it needs the expected word list).

## Problem

The existing `verify` stage performed no verification: it cloned each message and advanced `scrubState` to `verified`. Worse, `corpus scrub --stage verify --target <raw shards>` could read raw input directly and bless it one row at a time, without checking sibling shards, original-value provenance, deletion approval, canaries, attachment bytes, placeholders, or gitleaks.

## Change

- disables the row-level no-op; `corpus:scrub --stage all` now stops at `rewritten`, and direct `--stage verify` fails with a pointer to the corpus-wide command
- adds `corpus:verify`, a non-mutating, fail-closed `jsonl-text-v1` verifier
- snapshots the exact shard set, rejects concurrent shard/artifact changes and unknown JSON fields, and scans the same bytes with structured detectors and gitleaks
- requires an exact manifest plus unambiguous hash-chained ledger, recomputed complete mine candidates, original gazetteer, canary attestation, semantically validated deletion rules/review/approval artifacts, and placeholder registry
- scans every string-bearing message field with core structured PII detectors, regex entities, original-value gazetteer/LHS matching, and production redact patterns
- rejects embedded attachment bytes and malformed, legacy, forged, unregistered, or unused placeholders
- runs gitleaks over each exact shard with the repository config, a timeout, full redaction, mode-0600 transient reports, and fatal cleanup semantics
- emits a canonical self-hashed report containing hashes and structural locations only; no matched text, snippets, raw gitleaks secrets, or gazetteer values
- exports `assertFreshGreenVerification()` so #14773 reruns the complete gate and requires a byte-identical green report immediately before publishing; the self-hash is corruption detection, not authorization

This PR deliberately cannot certify the real corpus yet. #14769 must produce the required deletion approval/attachment disposition, production canary and placeholder-registry artifacts must exist, multimodal/audio verification remains outside the declared scope, and the owner must bind the ≥200-message review to the exact machine report hash.

- **Connections**: 36 services (all guarded-suite vars + the full `post-merge-secrets.txt` set — drift-guarded by a test); real read-only verify probes; Eliza Cloud device-code login (same protocol as `ElizaCloudClient.startCliLogin`); Google OAuth refresh-token mint via the console's own loopback callback, with hourly calendar-token re-mint before live runs.
- **Runner**: per-task `run-all-tests.mjs --filter='^<label>$' --min-tasks=1` spawns (keeps CI lane env/Postgres-provision/skip semantics), own process group for cancel, SSE live status, log-line-first result classification (exit 0 alone is not proof; exit 3 = vacuous-green skip).
- **Persistence**: `~/.eliza/test-console/` — `credentials.json` (0600), `runs/<id>/run.json` + per-task logs, `history.json` (re-run-failed survives restarts), `settings.json` (opt-in gates).

## What

`docker/certification/` runs the entire certification stack on one beefy Linux machine: container-parallel CPU test lanes + a pipelined GPU vision queue.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `compose.yml` | **Generated-then-committed** stack: `cpu` profile = one container per test lane with `cpuset` pinning + `cpus` quotas, read-only `/repo` mount, per-lane `scratch-*` volume, shared `build-cache`; `gpu` profile = one GPU-owning `gpu-vision` service (both resident llama-servers: Unlimited-OCR :8090 + Qwen3-VL :8091) + one `gpu-queue-worker` |
| `generate-compose-lanes.mjs` + `compose-lanes-lib.mjs` | Derives lane services from **`run-all-tests.mjs --plan=json --all`** — each `summary.byScript` script becomes a lane, big groups split with the runner's own `TEST_SHARD`, the plan's `cloudStep` becomes the `cloud` lane. **No second lane registry**; `--check` is the drift gate |
| `queue-lib.mjs` / `queue-worker.mjs` | Filesystem job queue (no redis/sqlite): claim-by-rename, max-pending backpressure on enqueue, drain-to-skip with honest `skipped` records once the GPU service is unreachable past a window. All state transitions pure + unit-tested |
| `certify-parallel.mjs` | Orchestrator: derive → `compose --profile cpu [--profile gpu] up` → per-lane exit codes/timings from `docker inspect` → `timings.json` whose `timings` field is `BundleMeta.timings`-compatible (`Record<phase, ms>`, packages/evidence). Deterministic degradation: no docker → serial fallback printed + **EXIT_NO_DOCKER=4**; compose drift → 5; timeout → 6 |
| `lane-entry.sh` / `gpu-entry.sh` | Container entrypoints (rsync-to-scratch + shared bun cache; dual llama-server launch that dies loudly if either server exits) |
| `README.md` | Cores→lane mapping, VRAM budget (~6–10 GiB both models at Q4), GPU-service-over-HTTP doctrine with **MPS as escape hatch only** (MIG N/A on consumer cards), macOS native-path pointer, queue protocol, exit codes |

Coordination with #14548: services **reference** `ghcr.io/elizaos/certification-gpu` (overridable via `ELIZA_CERT_IMAGE`/`ELIZA_CERT_GPU_IMAGE`); no competing Dockerfile is defined here.

CI: `bun test docker/certification` added to `scenario-pr.yml` (dir is outside workspace test discovery), covering the drift gate so `compose.yml` cannot silently diverge from the plan. `turbo.json` gains `ELIZA_CERT_QUEUE_HOST` in `globalEnv` (biome `noUndeclaredEnvVars`).

## Problem

`#15929` serialized only the migration-target lookup+insert: the advisory lock was released when `createTierUpgradeTarget` committed, while managed credential minting, environment writes, the worker-health rollback delete, and `enqueueAgentProvisionOnce` stayed route-level work. A losing concurrent request polled 10s for a job, then independently minted credentials and overwrote the target's environment; the fresh-target compensation wrapper could delete a target already owned by a committed provision job; the target insert hand-assembled `agentSandboxes` values instead of using the canonical builder.

## Fix (retains the #16042 shape the review asked to keep, plus its two blockers)

**One durable single-flight boundary** — `createTierUpgradeTargetWithProvision` (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/agent-tier-upgrade-target.ts`):

- **Phase 1 (locked tx):** reattach fast-path + pre-mint quota refusal.
- **Phase 2 (unlocked):** managed environment prepared against a pre-generated target id (the api-key mint runs on its own connection; a candidate key is bound to its caller's own prospective id, never the winner's target).
- **Phase 3 (locked tx, the boundary):** re-check → org-serialized quota assert → target insert through the canonical `buildAgentSandboxInsertValues` builder with the fully-prepared, storage-encrypted environment → **provision job insert in the same transaction** (`provisioningJobService.enqueueAgentProvisionOnceInTx`). Target + job are atomic; the compensation delete is gone; the 10s job poll is gone; worker health is checked before anything durable is minted.

**Blocker 1 — org quota serialization (closing review §1):** both phases acquire the **org-wide `elizaAgentCreateAdvisoryLockSql` BEFORE the per-source tier-upgrade lock** (global order: org → tier-upgrade → provision, documented in `eliza-provision-lock.ts`), so the count→insert window is atomic against ordinary `createAgent`, coding-container creates, and upgrades of a **different** source agent. Regressions: two different-source upgrades racing the last slot, and an upgrade racing `createAgent` at cap-1 — exactly one succeeds in each, proven on PGlite **and on real multi-connection Postgres 16**.

**Blocker 2 — ambiguous-commit credential ownership (closing review §2):** a boundary-transaction rejection is no longer treated as proof of rollback. `resolveOutcomeAfterBoundaryRejection` re-reads durable state on a fresh connection and only then acts:
- candidate id IS the live target → the commit landed; the **committed target+job are recovered and returned**, credential untouched;
- a competitor's target is live → candidate provably unreferenced → revoked, reattach;
- provably absent → revoked, original error stands;
- **verification itself fails → the credential is PRESERVED** (a stranded key is recoverable hygiene debt, #16071; a revoked live-target key breaks the agent) and the uncertainty is logged with both errors.

Typed errors: `ElizaError` codes `TIER_UPGRADE_TARGET_INSERT_FAILED` and `PROVISION_ENQUEUE_AGENT_NOT_FOUND` (message preserved for the routes that map "Agent not found" to 404). Known residual (crash between phase 2 and 3 strands a candidate api-key row with no GC path — pre-existing on the old compensation path too): tracked in #16071.

**Test infrastructure shipped with this** (the coverage lane co-runs every changed suite in ONE bun process, which surfaced two real hazards): module-scope `mock.module` calls execute at preload and clobber the shared `db/helpers`→`db/client` re-export binding under every other suite — all touched suites now install mocks in `beforeAll` and restore from value snapshots in `afterAll`; and drizzle-kit `pushSchema` answers internal errors with a silent `process.exit(1)` — the tier-upgrade suites apply plain DDL (`__tests__/tier-upgrade-pglite-schema.ts`, the `jobs-recovery.test.ts` pattern). Pre-existing eliza-sandbox/provisioning-jobs suites gained genuine cases (builder parity, quota boundary, dispatch payload contract, sweep completeness, failed-turn reservation release, bootstrap window for migration targets, profile/env update semantics), which also carries every changed source file past the tightened per-file LCOV floor (#16038).

## Proof against real multi-connection Postgres (closing review §3)

Disposable `postgres:16` container (`docker run -d -p 5544:5432 …`), fresh databases per run — **not** PGlite:

- **Full single-flight suite (14 tests) on Postgres 16**: the 6-way concurrent burst, the 10.5s delayed winner, both cap-1 quota races, commit-ack-loss recovery and verification-failure preservation all run as genuinely parallel transactions on separate pooled connections with real `pg_advisory_xact_lock` contention → 14 pass / 0 fail. Artifact: [15943-v2-pg-service-suite.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence/15943-v2-pg-service-suite.log)
- **Five concurrent HTTP POSTs through the real route** (real service, repositories, credential mint, job enqueue; auth is the only mocked seam) → all 202, exactly one `created:true`, all five converge on one target id + one job id; row dump shows 1 target / 1 `agent_provision` job / 1 `agent-sandbox:<target>` key. Artifact: [15943-v2-pg-route-5x-concurrent.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence/15943-v2-pg-route-5x-concurrent.log)
- **Failure injection at the commit and enqueue boundaries** runs in the same suite on both engines: enqueue-throw → full rollback (no target/job/key residue) + retry converges; commit-ack-loss → durable pair recovered with live credential; verification-failure → credential preserved, uncertainty surfaced.

**Staging E2E (honest status):** the real-Postgres multi-session proof above is attached; a deployed staging run of five concurrent HTTP requests through the hosted API + provisioning worker needs a credentialed staging deploy this lane does not have. Offered as an immediate follow-up if access is granted.

Infra/security-sensitive — flagged for review, not solo-merge.f7:T1638,## What & why

Closes #14781 (child of epic #14749; part of #14747).

Every artifact disclosure surface today collapses to OWNER at the HTTP
boundary, so any authenticated caller gets the full artifact. This adds
**per-viewer DTO selection** for shared artifacts — transcripts, stored files,
chat-message attachments, and meeting sessions — designed **inside the #8876
attachments doctrine**:

- Bytes stay **pre-auth** on the content-addressed store (the sha256 URL is the
  capability); "permission" == URL/DTO disclosure on the **referencing record**,
  never a byte-serve gate.
- **Redacted variants are separate media objects** under their own sha256
  (`Media.redactedUrl`), never an edit of the original, never a `fileId`.
- **ONE predicate** decides disclosure everywhere.

## Design decisions

**Core — one predicate, three outcomes** (`packages/core/src/access-control/artifact-disclosure.ts`):
`resolveArtifactDisclosure(record, ctx, agentId) -> "full" | "redacted" | "none"`.
Ordering: no access context (single-owner local boundary) -> full (documented,
unchanged); agent-self / OWNER / ADMIN-rank -> full; an explicit per-entity grant
wins **both** ways (a `full` grant elevates past the scope ladder, a `redacted`
grant narrows even a `global`-scope record so an owner's "redact for this viewer"
cannot be undone by a coarse scope); otherwise the scope ladder (`canReadScope`),
which fails closed on the `owner-private` default. `parseArtifactShareGrants`
sanitizes `metadata.share.grants` at the jsonb boundary (malformed -> grants
nothing).

**Grants ride additively on the referencing record** (`metadata.share.grants`)
— zero migration, no sha256-keyed table (respects doctrine AD1). This PR
implements the **read** side; the grant **write** path (share actions,
room-snapshot capture) is #14778/#14779's.

**DTO selection lives in use-cases, not routes** (repo rule: clients render,
never compute) — `transcript-store.ts`, `plugin-meetings/session-disclosure.ts`,
`agent/api/files-disclosure.ts`, `agent/api/attachment-disclosure.ts`. Routes
only assemble.

**Per-user HTTP principal via the existing seam** — a new
`artifact-share-role-resolver` registers through the #12087 `TokenRoleResolver`
seam (WaifuChat precedent): signed share-viewer tokens (USER/GUEST only,
GET-only artifact allowlist, inert without a secret). `resolveHttpAccessContext`
maps the boundary principal to `AccessContext`; dispatch threads it to route
handlers. The trunk-authorized local owner resolves **no** context, so the
single-owner dashboard is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**GC safety** — `collectReferencedMedia` now scans `redactedUrl` so the daily
sweep keeps redacted variants alive.

## Flagged / skipped (dependencies I did not implement)

- **Grant write path** (share/redact actions, room-snapshot capture) is
  #14778/#14779; this PR only *reads* `metadata.share.grants` + the
  `redactedVariantId`/`redactionOf` variant links. Tests seed those directly.
- **#14777 (owner doctrine decisions) is `needs-shaw`** — I implemented only the
  default matrix the issue itself specifies (AGENT/ADMIN/OWNER full;
  USER/GUEST grant-driven). No signed-byte-URL / byte-revocation / AD1-reopen
  capability was built (D1-D3 recommended *decline*); if D4/D5 ratify
  differently, only the ordering in `resolveArtifactDisclosure` changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- Contract tests per role x surface (OWNER full / ADMIN full / USER-redacted
  sees variant + flag / USER-ungranted omitted / GUEST omitted). Done.
- Zero client-side redaction logic — grep-clean (`RedactedBadge` is
  display-only; the server stamps `redacted`). Done.
- Three-state rule (denied != empty != error): Files `restricted` state. Done.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)f8:T1b29,## What & why

**PR-2 of the web-push lane** (PWA optimization dossier §3). PR-1 (#15185) landed the browser half — the service-worker `push`/`notificationclick` handlers, the gesture-gated subscription manager, and the `webPushVapidPublicKey` boot-config placeholder. This PR builds the **cloud SENDER** half so a closed/installed iOS PWA actually receives a notification when the agent replies.

iOS 16.4+ supports web push only for installed PWAs and rides APNs transparently via standard VAPID/`PushManager` — no Apple SDK. The entire crypto + send path here is **WebCrypto-only** so it runs unmodified on Cloudflare Workers (node `web-push` won't).

## What's in this PR

**VAPID config plumbing**
- `webPushVapidPublicKey` is injected into served HTML via the existing boot-config seed (`static-file-server.ts`), read from `ELIZA_WEB_PUSH_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`. The public key is safe for the browser (it's the `applicationServerKey`).
- The **private** key is a cloud secret (`ELIZA_WEB_PUSH_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`), read only server-side; it is never injected, logged, or committed. `getWebPushVapidConfig` returns `null` when unconfigured so a cluster without keys simply no-ops.

**Subscription store — `POST`/`DELETE /api/v1/web-push/subscriptions`**
- Persists the browser's `PushSubscription.toJSON()` keyed to `(user, agent)`. **Uniqueness is the composite `(endpoint, agent_id)`** so a single installed PWA can subscribe to multiple agents without one agent's subscribe clobbering another's row.
- Endpoints are **SSRF-guarded**: only `https` URLs to public hosts are stored (localhost / loopback / private / link-local `169.254.169.254` metadata / IPv6 literals / internal TLDs are rejected), since the sender later POSTs to whatever is stored.
- DELETE is scoped to the authed user.

**Cloudflare-Workers-compatible sender (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/web-push`)**
- VAPID JWT signing (ES256 over P-256, raw `r||s` — the JWS format, not DER) via `crypto.subtle`.
- aes128gcm payload encryption (RFC 8188 content coding + RFC 8291 Web Push key derivation) via `crypto.subtle` HKDF/ECDH/AES-GCM.
- Fetch-based send with `TTL`/`Urgency` headers; **prunes subscriptions that return 404/410 Gone**.

**Agent-reply → push hook**
- On a completed reply with no live foreground client for that `(user, agent)`, enqueues a web-push and sets `badgeCount`. Wired at the `/api/v1/agents/[agentId]/message` completed branch, registered with **`executionCtx.waitUntil`** so the Worker keeps the send + prune alive after the chat response returns.

## Tests (bun + vitest — 91 green)
- VAPID JWT: signs, verifies under the public key, correct claims, raw 64-byte `r||s`, rejects malformed keys.
- aes128gcm: correct header framing + **full UA-private-key decrypt round-trip** + deterministic-with-injected-salt.
- Sender: 2xx=ok, 404/410=gone(prune), 500/network=keep, malformed endpoint=gone-without-fetch; batch collects `goneEndpoints`.
- notify-service: no-push-when-unconfigured / foreground-active / no-subscriptions; prunes gone; never throws.
- SSRF guard: accepts Apple/FCM/Mozilla, rejects http/localhost/private/metadata/IPv6.
- Migration shape: composite unique index (not endpoint-only), cascade, journal + barrel registration.
- HTML injection: seeds the VAPID public key, merges with apiBase into one write, never leaks when absent.
- Routes: store/validate/delete + all SSRF cases.

f9:T2fe7,## What & why

Closes #15796 — a newly spun-up agent (cloud container, fresh desktop install, new user) had no guided path to GitHub credentials, so every GitHub-touching capability (`TASKS_MANAGE_ISSUES`, `TASKS_SUBMIT_WORKSPACE`, repo provisioning) failed until the operator discovered the right setting by reading source.

This makes GitHub credentials a **first-class guided setup step**, reusing the #15749 device-flow primitive as promised in the claim: the Settings → Coding Agents **GitHub connection card** now offers *Sign in with GitHub* (OAuth device flow) alongside the existing PAT paste, stores the obtained token **per-agent via runtime settings + the existing credential store (not process env)**, and mid-task credential failures now point at the setup step.

**Complementary PR:** #15844 (same issue, docs slice for `plugin-agent-orchestrator` README) is open from a parallel lane — zero file overlap with this PR (this PR touches `workspace-github.ts` source + `packages/docs/connectors/github.md`; that one touches the orchestrator README/CLAUDE/AGENTS).

**Out of scope (owner decision pending, per the claim):** the cloud per-agent identity policy — bot account vs user PAT vs GitHub App installation for cloud-provisioned agents. Noted as an open question in the docs; not decided here.

**`elizaos` CLI:** intentionally **not** added. Per `packages/elizaos/CLAUDE.md` the CLI is a standalone, dependency-light scaffolding tool that does not import the runtime; the device flow needs the running agent's HTTP surface and per-agent settings, so a CLI login step would bloat it with runtime/server concerns for no benefit. The dashboard card is the guided surface.

## Changes

**`@elizaos/plugin-github`**
- New `src/device-flow.ts` — TypeScript port of the #15749 primitive (`scripts/lifeops/github-device-login.mjs`): `device_code` never leaves the server, server-owned polling interval (honors `slow_down`, throttles eager clients locally), 409 owner-setup vs 502 upstream error taxonomy, expiry sweep — plus one addition: **flows are bound to the agent that started them** (`agentKey`), so on a multi-agent host one agent's runtime can never poll another agent's flow.
- Two new routes: `POST /api/github/device/start` (409 with an actionable owner-setup message when `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` is absent) and `POST /api/github/device/poll` (`pending`/`denied`/`expired`, or on grant: validate against GitHub `/user` → persist via the existing `github-credentials` store → apply to the live runtime per-agent via `setSetting("GITHUB_TOKEN", …, true)`). No second storage mechanism; no process-env write (env leaks to every agent on a multi-tenant host — the existing boot-time `applySavedTokenToEnv` behavior for `gh`/`git` subprocess inheritance is unchanged).
- `GET /api/github/token` now reports `deviceFlowAvailable`; the PAT `POST` also applies the live runtime setting (connect → retry works without a restart); `DELETE` disconnects the live runtime too.
- **Latent bug fixed:** `readJsonBody` now prefers the canonical dispatcher's pre-parsed `req.body` — an `application/json` POST (the exact shape the dashboard card sends) previously read an already-consumed stream and returned 400 through `tryHandleRuntimePluginRoute` (the existing e2e dodged it by posting `text/plain`, with a comment acknowledging the behavior). Covered by a new test that posts real `application/json` through the real dispatcher.
- `action-helpers.needsClientError` now points at the setup card, not just env var names.

**`@elizaos/plugin-task-coordinator`**
- `GitHubConnectionCard` grows the guided path: *Sign in with GitHub* → prominent short code + `github.com/login/device` link (opened externally) → poll at the server-provided cadence → connected; denied/expired resolve to actionable errors with the PAT fallback suggested; Cancel really stops the poll loop (generation-guarded timers, cleaned on unmount). Orange accent only, no blue, accent → darker-accent hover (kit `Button` variants).
- New real-browser screenshot harness `src/__e2e__/{github-card-fixture.tsx, build-github-card-fixture.mjs, run-github-card-shot.mjs}` (modeled on the existing `run-dashboard-shot.mjs`; build under bun, drive under node).

**`@elizaos/plugin-agent-orchestrator`**
- `workspace-github.ts` missing-credential errors now point at Settings → Coding Agents (the mid-task failure → setup-step UX from the issue).

**Docs**
- `packages/docs/connectors/github.md`: new *Guided credential setup (dashboard)* section — PAT vs device sign-in comparison, **vault/settings vs env** (multi-tenant leak warning), and the open cloud identity-policy note.
- plugin-github + plugin-task-coordinator `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (kept identical) + plugin-github README updated for the new routes/card.

## What ships

| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/vast/run-certification.mjs` | Plain-node vast driver (zero workspace imports): search offers (`RTX_4090`, `num_gpus 1`, `verified`, `reliability2>0.98`, `inet_down>500`, sort `dph+`, `dph<=--max-dph`) → create from `ghcr.io/elizaos/certification-gpu:latest` → onstart clones the repo @ `--sha` and runs `bundle:create → certify:rollup → certify:sign` → poll `actual_status` (`exited`/`unknown`/`offline` debounced, stuck-`loading` cap, hard `--timeout-minutes`) → pull the signed cert via instance logs → **DESTROY in `finally`** (never stop; 3 retries; loud instance-id banner + exit 12 if destroy fails) |
| `scripts/vast/run-certification.test.mjs` | 36 unit tests over the pure pieces (offer filter/sort, onstart assembly + 16 KB guard, poll state machine, budget guards, secret redaction, auth-error classification) — `bun run test:vast` |
| `scripts/vast/local-certify.mjs` | One-command local fallback: same chain, same signed output; `--no-sign` stops after rollup for hand review |
| `scripts/vast/README.md` | Runbook: local fallback, costs, kill-path table (one distinct exit code per kill path) |
| `docker/certification/Dockerfile.gpu` | Bakes CUDA `llama-server` (pinned llama.cpp `b8525`, the `scripts/gpu-vision` minimum), sha256-pinned OCR/VLM models via the repo's `setup.mjs --with-vlm`, Node 24, Bun 1.3.14, Playwright Chromium + deps, tesseract, ffmpeg — everything the 16 KB onstart cannot carry |
| `.github/workflows/certification-image.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` + develop-push path trigger; GHCR push via `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`packages: write`); tags `latest` + `sha-<short>` |
| `.github/workflows/certification-vast.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` (sha/tier/max_dph/max_attempts/timeout inputs) + nightly cron gated on `vars.ELIZA_VAST_CERT_ENABLED == 'true'`; **no `pull_request` trigger**; secrets exposed only to the single run step; any failure goes red with a "local certification required: `node scripts/vast/local-certify.mjs --tier full`" summary |

## Design points

- **Secrets discipline:** `ELIZA_CERT_SIGNING_KEY` + optional `CERT_PUSH_CMD` travel only in the create-payload env (docker `-e`), never in the onstart text, logs, or `--dry-run` output (unit-tested). The onstart is printable and safe.
- **Budget guards:** `--max-dph` (server-side `lte` + client-side re-check), `--max-attempts` across offers cheapest-first; retries fire only on host-side failures (stuck loading / instance lost / create rejected), never on chain failures or timeouts. Worst case per dispatch: `0.60 × 3 × 2h = $3.60`; each run logs its estimated spend.
- **Live-API verification without spend:** vast rejects a dead key with **HTTP 404 + `{"error":"auth_error"}`** (not 401), and search offers is `PUT /search/asks/` with a `{q: ...}` body (`select_cols: ["*"]` is rejected by the current API). Both discovered against the live API and encoded + unit-tested; the dead-key kill path is verified live below.
- **Results without storage:** the signed `certification.json` is emitted between log markers and recovered from the pulled instance logs, so a run is useful even before `ELIZA_CERT_PUSH_CMD` (R2/S3) is configured; the full bundle push stays env-driven.

--- onstart script ---
#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail
fail() { echo "ELIZA-CERT-RUN-FAILURE: $1"; exit 1; }
echo "[cert-run] begin sha=b7247c66c7a5a8cdfa38a33e98f68dc71ccd8680 tier=full"
export HOME=${HOME:-/root}
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
export ELIZA_EVIDENCE_RUNNER=vast
mkdir -p /workspace && cd /workspace || fail workspace
rm -rf eliza && mkdir eliza && cd eliza
git init -q -b certification || fail git-init
git remote add origin 'https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza.git' || fail git-remote
git fetch --depth 1 origin b7247c66c7a5a8cdfa38a33e98f68dc71ccd8680 || fail fetch-sha
git checkout -q FETCH_HEAD || fail checkout
bun run install:light || fail install
if command -v llama-server >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${ELIZA_GPU_VISION_CACHE:-}" ]; then
  node scripts/gpu-vision/serve.mjs --vlm --verify || fail gpu-vision-serve
else
  echo "[cert-run] gpu-vision service unavailable in this image; vision lanes will record as absent"
fi
bun run --cwd packages/evidence bundle:create -- --tier full || fail bundle-create
BUNDLE_DIR="$(ls -td "$PWD"/evidence/runs/*/ 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
[ -n "$BUNDLE_DIR" ] || fail bundle-dir
BUNDLE_DIR="${BUNDLE_DIR%/}"
bun run --cwd packages/evidence certify:rollup -- --bundle "$BUNDLE_DIR" --out "$BUNDLE_DIR/verdicts.json" || fail rollup
bun run --cwd packages/evidence certify:sign -- --bundle "$BUNDLE_DIR" --verdicts "$BUNDLE_DIR/verdicts.json" --reviewer-id 'vast-certification-runner' --reviewer-kind agent || fail sign
echo "-----BEGIN ELIZA CERTIFICATION JSON-----"
cat "$BUNDLE_DIR/certification.json" || fail cert-read
echo ""
echo "-----END ELIZA CERTIFICATION JSON-----"
if [ -n "${CERT_PUSH_CMD:-}" ]; then
  export CERT_BUNDLE_DIR="$BUNDLE_DIR"
  export CERT_FILE="$BUNDLE_DIR/certification.json"
  bash -c "$CERT_PUSH_CMD" || fail push
else
  echo "[cert-run] no CERT_PUSH_CMD configured; bundle stays on the instance (certification travels via logs)"
fi
echo "ELIZA-CERT-RUN-SUCCESS"


```

</details>

fe:T324b,Implements #15355 — the first-class shared→dedicated agent upgrade, per the cloud-hardening scoping comment on the issue (2026-07-09T01:44Z).

## What ships

**1. Backend — `POST /api/v1/eliza/agents/:agentId/upgrade-tier`** (new route; distinct from the `agent_upgrade`/`downgrade` image blue/green machinery)
- **Ownership + tier validation:** org-scoped read (cross-org indistinguishable from missing → 404, no oracle); only `execution_tier === 'shared'` upgrades (409 `not_shared_tier`); only a `running` source (409 `agent_not_running`).
- **Hosting-runway credit gate:** `checkAgentTierUpgradeCreditGate` requires balance above `AGENT_PRICING.UPGRADE_MINIMUM_BALANCE` ($0.72 = 3 days × `DAILY_RUNNING_COST` $0.24) — stricter than the $0.10 create minimum, because a dedicated agent burns credits continuously. Denials reuse the canonical `insufficientCredits402` body, now carrying the **enforced** threshold in `requiredBalance` (and the warn log reports the real threshold too).
- **Server-side identity copy:** `agent_name` / `character_id` / `agent_config` / `environment_vars` are read from the shared row on the server (the compat create route never reads the source row and clients can't reconstruct identity from DTOs). Platform-reserved env keys (`ELIZA_API_TOKEN`, `ELIZA_CLOUD_AGENT_ID`, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, …) are stripped so the target mints its own identity; user BYO env — including `enc:v1:` ciphertext — survives verbatim (same-org envelope key; the storage encryptor never double-encrypts).
- **Provisioning:** dedicated-always create under the balance-tiered org quota (`forceCreate` semantics; 429 on quota), managed env preparation, worker-health check at the enqueue boundary with explicit row rollback, real `agent_provision` job + 202 with the standard `polling` envelope. Create→enqueue failures roll the fresh row back (orphan-cleanup wrapper).
- **Retry idempotency, tier-checked:** the target records `__agentUpgradedFrom: <sharedId>` in the reserved `__agent` config namespace (client input can never forge it at create time — new `AGENT_UPGRADED_FROM_KEY` in `eliza-agent-config.ts`). A retried POST **reattaches** to the live in-flight target (2xx `alreadyInProgress: true`, same `dedicatedAgentId`, active job reused) instead of minting a second container. Reattach requires the candidate to be `execution_tier === 'dedicated-always'` — `agent_config` is PATCHable, so a marker planted on a non-dedicated row is never treated as a live target (covered by a route test that fails without the check).

**2. Client — chat continuity via the existing #15313 handoff stack**
- New `packages/ui/src/cloud/handoff/start-tier-upgrade.ts`: `runSharedToDedicatedUpgradeHandoff()` wraps `startCloudAgentHandoff` (readiness poll → idempotent transcript import; canonical conversation id === shared agent id) and deletes the shared bridge **only** on a confirmed `switched`/`switched-empty` — awaited and reported (`sharedBridgeDeleted`), never fire-and-forget. On `timed-out`/`failed` the user keeps the working shared agent and a retry resumes the same upgrade.

**3. UI — "Upgrade to Dedicated" on the agent detail page** (next to the #15639 deactivate flow, `packages/ui/src/cloud/instances/components/agent-actions.tsx`)
- Shared-tier-only action; confirm dialog spells out the continuous burn ($0.24/day, $0.01/hr) and the $0.72 / 3-days-of-hosting minimum **before** anything changes — figures from the same `AGENT_PRICING` constants the gate enforces (client only displays; a 402's message renders the server's numbers verbatim).
- Confirm fires the real POST; progress rides a reload-free `useJobPoller` instance (the default hard reload would kill the in-page transcript move) + a whole-span progress line; on a confirmed switch the page navigates to the dedicated agent; a failed shared-bridge delete is surfaced, not hidden. i18n catalog entries added (`en.json`).

## Design notes

- **Naming trap respected:** the existing `agent_upgrade` job / `downgrade` route are image blue/green — this route is `upgrade-tier` and mints a new record, per the issue scoping.
- **Reattach over dedupe-by-lock:** the marker scan is best-effort dedup for real retry shapes (double-click, reload, second tab); a sub-second concurrent race is bounded by the per-org agent quota enforced under the create's advisory lock. Only a `dedicated-always` row can be reattached to — the marker alone is not proof of a migration target.
- **Reattach skips the credit gate** deliberately: nothing new is minted, and gating it would strand a user whose balance dipped after the (gated) mint while the container is already billing — ongoing solvency belongs to the billing cron + low-credit shutdown.
- **Warm pool skipped** on the upgrade path: upgrades are not latency-critical and always take the async job path (comment in route).
- Downgrade story stays suspend / deactivate / delete (shown in the confirm copy); true tier-downgrade (reverse transcript export) does not exist today and is out of scope per the issue scoping.

ff:Tf13,Closes #13534

## What

Replaces the recency-truncated `ILIKE '%query%'` chat-message search (defects #1/#2 of #13534) with **corpus-wide ranking in the store**. A new `IDatabaseAdapter.searchMessages` runs a GIN-indexed Postgres FTS query (`websearch_to_tsquery` + `ts_rank_cd`) over a folded `eliza_message_search_document` (message body + attachment titles/urls), with an optional `pg_trgm` GIN fallback for partial/typo/URL/emoji/CJK tokens the FTS lexer misses. Room-scoping, `agentId`, and `LIMIT/OFFSET` are all applied **in SQL, after ranking**, so a relevant hit older than any recency window is still found and ordered.

Implemented on three adapters — Drizzle (`plugin-sql`), core in-memory, and `plugin-inmemorydb` — with a JS fold twin (`foldForSearch` / `rankMessageSearch` in `packages/core/src/search.ts`) so in-memory results stay behaviorally aligned with Postgres (café/cafe, don't/dont, attachment-filename hits). The conversation-search route ranks in the store; the response DTO is unchanged, so the existing `MessageSearchPanel` + jump-to-message UI work as-is.

## Key files

- `packages/core/src/types/database.ts`, `database.ts`, `runtime.ts` — `MessageSearchHit` type + `searchMessages` on the adapter interface and runtime delegate
- `packages/core/src/search.ts` — `foldForSearch`, `messageSearchDocument`, `rankMessageSearch` (JS twin)
- `plugins/plugin-sql/src/message-search.ts`, `base.ts`, `migration-service.ts` — SQL FTS/trigram objects + adapter impl, installed idempotently post-migration
- `packages/core/src/database/inMemoryAdapter.ts`, `plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts` — in-memory impls
- `packages/agent/src/api/conversation-routes.ts` — route ranks via `searchMessages`
- `packages/benchmarks/searchbench/` — 10k-corpus KPI harness + budgets
